description: Running number over the entity master data table, assigned in LEI order at each rebuild; dense but not stable across rebuilds.
For an investment fund on the ECB investment fund register, its investment policy as stated in the register (e.g. equity, bond or mixed fund).
For an investment fund on the ECB register, its fund type: ETF, PEF (private equity fund) or 'Neither ETF nor PEF' (renamed from 'Type of investment fund' and abbreviated).
For an investment fund on the ECB register, whether it is UCITS compliant: UCITS, or AIF for a non-UCITS alternative investment fund (renamed from 'UCITS compliance' and abbreviated).

Legal Entity Identifier (ISO 17442) of the entity, normalised the way GLEIF writes it (blanks removed, upper case); in the GLEIF Level 2 relationship data it is read from the start node of the relationship.

Sector of the entity, taken from the narrowest sectoral register it appears in: CCP (ESMA CCP list), INUN (EIOPA insurance undertaking), ORPI (EIOPA IORP), CB/CDTI/OFI/MMF or MFI (ECB MFI list, by category), or UCIT/AIFD/INVF (ECB investment fund register, by UCITS compliance).
Refinement of SECTOR offered by the register that set it: the type of CCP (EUCCP, T1CCP, T2CCP) for CCPs, or the investment policy for funds whose sector comes from the ECB fund register.
ISO 4217 code of the base currency of the rate: EUR for ECB and (converted) BIS rates, or the rebase currency where the table is rebased.
Helper column: the rate used to convert a series, i.e. the EUR to rebase-currency rate on the same date (renamed from VALUE), or in the BIS conversion the EUR/USD rate; dropped from the final table.
Helper column: whether the EUR to rebase-currency rate used for rebasing on that date was itself carried forward from an earlier day (renamed from IMPUTED); dropped from the final table.

True where the day carries the last available rate of the pair from an earlier day (e.g. weekends, TARGET closing days) rather than a rate quoted on that day; after rebasing, also true where the conversion rate was imputed.
ISO 4217 code of the quoted currency (for BIS data the first three characters of the currency field).
Reference date of the rate, one row per calendar day in the Silver table (from 'Date' in ECB data, 'TIME_PERIOD' in BIS data).
Source of the rate: ECB, BIS, or whatever the proprietary (internal) rate file states; where several sources quote a pair on a date, internal takes precedence over ECB and ECB over BIS.
Kind of rate: 'ref' for ECB euro foreign exchange reference rates, 'avg' for BIS daily average rates, or as stated in the internal file.
Exchange rate: units of QUOTE per one unit of BASE. BIS USD-based rates are converted to EUR-based ones by multiplying with EUR/USD, and a rebase divides by the EUR to rebase-currency rate.

Action type: the delta-file element a record was reported in, NewRcrd (new), ModfdRcrd (modified), TermntdRcrd (terminated) or CancRcrd (cancelled); it determines how the record changes the instrument history.
Date and time the issuer approved the admission to trading or trading of its instrument on the venue (RTS 23 field 9, date of approval of the admission to trading).
Classification of the instrument as an ISO 10962 CFI code (RTS 23 field 3). In the compact table, the distinct codes reported by the venues for an ISIN joined with '+'.
Commodity derivative indicator: whether the instrument is a commodity derivative (RTS 23 field 4).
Reference date of the FIRDS file (Bronze partition) a record was read from, i.e. the publication date of the full or delta file.
Seniority of a debt instrument (RTS 23 field 23): SNDB senior, MZZD mezzanine, SBOD subordinated or JUND junior.
Delivery type of a derivative (RTS 23 field 34): PHYS physical, CASH cash or OPTL optional.
Date and time of admission to trading or of the first trade on the venue (RTS 23 field 11).
Full name of the financial instrument (RTS 23 field 2).
Identifier of the reference rate (index or benchmark) of a floating rate debt instrument: its ISIN, index code or name, according to INTRSTRATEFLTGIDTP (RTS 23 fields 19 and 20).
How the reference rate of a floating rate debt instrument is identified in INTRSTRATEFLTGID: ISIN, Index (index code) or Name; derived from which of the three elements is filled.
Spread in basis points over the reference rate of a floating rate debt instrument (RTS 23 field 22).
Unit of the term of the floating reference rate (RTS 23 field 21): DAYS, WEEK, MNTH or YEAR.
Number of units of the term of the floating reference rate (RTS 23 field 21), e.g. 3 for a three-month rate.
Fixed interest (coupon) rate of a debt instrument, in percent (RTS 23 field 18).
Instrument identification code: the ISIN of the financial instrument (RTS 23 field 1).
Whether the admission to trading or trading on the venue was requested or approved by the issuer (RTS 23 field 8).
LEI of the issuer, or of the trading venue operator where the instrument has no issuer (RTS 23 field 5). In the compact table, the distinct values across venues joined with '+'.

Whether the version is the most recent one received for its instrument, i.e. the LATESTRECORD flag of section 4.2 of ESMA65-8-5014. One version of an instrument carries it at a time, which is what the first query of section 4.3 selects on.
In the FIRDS watermark (metadata) table, the reference date of the newest file applied to the named table. The update applies every delta file newer than it and none that is older.
Maturity date of a debt instrument (RTS 23 field 15). In the compact table, the value the venues agree on, empty where they disagree.
In the FIRDS watermark (metadata) table, the table of the Silver layer the row records the watermark of, e.g. MAIN. The table holds one row per such table.
Nominal value per unit, or minimum traded value, of a debt instrument (RTS 23 field 17).
Currency of the nominal value per unit of a debt instrument (ISO 4217).
Notional currency of the instrument (RTS 23 field 13, notional currency 1), ISO 4217.

Tag naming what an incoming record does to the version in force, CLOSE_AND_INSERT or REPLACE. It is attached to the plan a delta file implies, which the merge of the Silver layer reads and no table stores.
Option exercise style (RTS 23 field 33): EURO, AMER, ASIA, BERM or OTHR.
Option type (RTS 23 field 30): CALL, PUTO or OTHR.
Price multiplier of a derivative: the number of units of the underlying represented by one contract (RTS 23 field 25). In the compact table, the value the venues agree on, empty where they disagree.
Date and time of the request for admission to trading on the venue (RTS 23 field 10).
Short name of the instrument, the ISO 18774 FISN (RTS 23 field 7). In the compact table, the distinct names across venues joined with '+'.

Technical attribute: start of the record's publication period in FIRDS, from whichever branch of the period is stated (FrDt, FrDtToDt.FrDt or Dt), falling back to the file's reference date for terminations and cancellations that state no period.
Technical attribute: end of the record's publication period in FIRDS, stated for records whose publication has ended (terminations).
Technical attribute: the relevant competent authority for the instrument, as a two-letter country code.
Technical attribute: MIC of the relevant trading venue, the most relevant market in terms of liquidity for the instrument.
Termination date: date and time the instrument ceases to be traded or admitted to trading on the venue (RTS 23 field 12).
Total issued nominal amount of a debt instrument (RTS 23 field 14).
Currency of the total issued nominal amount of a debt instrument (ISO 4217; RTS 23 field 16, currency of nominal value).
Trading venue: the MIC of the venue the instrument is admitted to or traded on (RTS 23 field 6). In the compact table, the distinct venues of an ISIN joined with '+'.
In the FIRDS watermark (metadata) table, the timestamp at which the newest file (MAXDATE) was last applied to the named table.
First day the version of the instrument is valid on, taken from the start of the publication period as section 4.2 of ESMA65-8-5014 prescribes.
Last day the version of the instrument is valid on, empty while the version is the one in force. A superseded version is closed on the day before the version that replaced it begins.
Expiry date of a derivative (RTS 23 field 24). In the compact table, the value the venues agree on, empty where they disagree.
